races.title: State Assembly, District 14
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Mark Rendon
cands.bio: Green Party candidate for California Assembly District 14 in 2026. Educator and musician who taught music for 29 years in the Oakland Unified School District. Served as a site representative, executive board member, treasurer and secretary of the Oakland Education Association. Has held no public office.

endorsements.text: Green Party of California, Green Party of Alameda County, Green Party of Contra Costa County, California Peace and Freedom Party and Our Revolution East Bay, as listed in his Ballotpedia survey response. He also lists individuals including boona cheema and Orlando Johnson.
Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations from Berkeley Progressives, El Sobrante Grab them by the Ballot Party, and Greens for US (Sway voting groups).

cands.gaps: We found no record of Rendon holding public office, so there are no legislative actions to report. We did not find his stated positions on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, abortion, or gun purchase rules and red-flag laws. We found no independent news coverage of his campaign. His birth in Sacramento, upbringing in Washington, DC, and teaching career come from his own Ballotpedia survey and campaign site, not from independent records. The year he moved back to California is not stated.

local.label: Roots 90: Rendon says he was born in Sacramento but grew up in Washington, DC. He returned to California for graduate study at UC Berkeley (degree 1990) and then taught in Oakland schools for 29 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Taught music for 29 years in the Oakland Unified School District. Held elected union positions in the Oakland Education Association (site rep, executive board, treasurer, secretary) and served as a delegate to the California Teachers Association State Council. Holds a graduate degree in education administration from UC Berkeley. Has never held public office.
qual.why: He has a long career as a public school teacher and union officer, which is only loosely related to writing law and budgets. He has no legislative service and no policy or budget career, so he lands in the low-to-middle range.
qual.label: He has a long career as a public school teacher and union officer, which is only loosely related to writing law and budgets. He has no legislative service and no policy or budget career, so he lands in the low-to-middle range.

stop-data-centers.evidence: His campaign priorities list includes a statewide ban on hyperscale data centers.

clean-money.evidence: He says he refuses corporate and super PAC donations and, as a Green, accepts no corporate or PAC money. He also supports banning corporations and super PACs from funding campaigns.

workers-first.evidence: He calls for abolishing ICE, closing its detention centers, and covering every resident with healthcare regardless of immigration status.

back-police-order.evidence: He supports ending the criminalization of homelessness, replacing school police with counseling professionals, and replacing the carceral system with restorative justice.

second-amendment.evidence: He supports a statewide ban on Flock cameras and stronger privacy protections.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: He supports recruiting, retaining and fairly compensating educators and school staff. His priorities also call for fully funded free public education, with no mention of vouchers or charters.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: He supports transforming refineries to renewable energy, blocking the proposed coal port in Oakland, and Indigenous-led land management. He also supports closing developer tax loopholes tied to affordable housing mandates.

prio.label: Matches 5 of 7 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 5 only promised

roots.summary: Rendon says he was born in Sacramento but grew up in Washington, DC. He returned to California for graduate study at UC Berkeley (degree 1990) and then taught in Oakland schools for 29 years.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign priorities list: "Implement a statewide ban on hyperscale data centers."

cands.name: Buffy Wicks
cands.bio: Democrat representing California Assembly District 14 (Berkeley, Richmond and nearby East Bay cities). First elected in 2018. Previously deputy director of the White House Office of Public Engagement under President Obama, executive director of Priorities USA Action, and founder of Rise Strategies. Chairs the Assembly Appropriations Committee.

endorsements.text: 2026: Democratic Party of California, SEIU Local 521, IUOE Local 3, Equality California and YIMBY Action, among others listed by Ballotpedia.
2018: Barack Obama endorsed her in the general election.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from Wicks on data centers, eliminating homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, immigration enforcement or H-1B, police pay and pensions or penalties for public disorder, gun policy, or school choice and teacher pay. Her Ballotpedia profile says she did not complete its 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, so her only stated positions in the sources are from 2018. We could not confirm the exact bill numbers or outcomes of her housing bills beyond what Wikipedia summarizes. We did not find her place of upbringing named beyond 'a small town in Northern California' and her Placer High School graduation.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says she was born in Foresthill, California and graduated from Placer High School in 1995, and her 2018 Ballotpedia survey says she grew up in a small town in rural Northern California and attended public schools from kindergarten through college.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Member of the California Assembly since 2018 (re-elected through 2026), including a term chairing the Housing and Community Development Committee and a current Appropriations chair. Earlier she was deputy director of the White House Office of Public Engagement, executive director of Priorities USA Action, a campaign director at Common Sense Kids Action, and founder of Rise Strategies, LLC.
qual.why: Several terms of legislative service plus a policy and political-strategy career put her in the high band for writing law and budgets. The committee chair roles were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: Several terms of legislative service plus a policy and political-strategy career put her in the high band for writing law and budgets. The committee chair roles were not counted toward the score.

pro-life.evidence: Introduced AB 2223, which would bar civil or criminal liability for a person's actions or omissions regarding pregnancy outcomes, including miscarriage, stillbirth or abortion.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Sponsored 2025 legislation to exempt most urban housing developments from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).

prio.label: Matches 0 of 2 priorities; 2 backed by their record, 0 only promised

roots.summary: Wikipedia says she was born in Foresthill, California and graduated from Placer High School in 1995, and her 2018 Ballotpedia survey says she grew up in a small town in rural Northern California and attended public schools from kindergarten through college.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In her 2018 Ballotpedia survey she listed housing as her top priority and pledged to 'build more transit-oriented affordable homes for low-income people more quickly' and to 'grow in a smart way by building more homes in walkable, transit-oriented neighborhoods.'
